rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع عن انكار البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it rebukes the Messenger for haste and censures that haste.
rows.anchor: ردع لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن العجلة وإنكار لها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's children love worldly life and its desires because they were created and disposed to haste, rushing in everything.
rows.anchor: كأنه قبل بل أنتم يا بني آدم لأنكم خلقتم من عجل وطبعتم عليه تعجلون في كل شيء ومن ثم تحبون العاجلة الدنيا وشهواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They abandon the afterlife, its abode and delights, and do not work for it.
rows.anchor: الدار الآخرة ونعيمها فلا تعملون لها

rows.speaker: مدني وكوفي
rows.claim: Medinese and Kufan readers use tāʾ in the verbs of both verses.
rows.anchor: والقراءة فيهما بالتاء مدني وكوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes preferring this world over the afterlife and tells people to desist.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع عن ايثار الدنيا على الآخرة كأنه قبل ارتدعوا عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He urges preparation for imminent death: the present life ends then, and people pass to an everlasting afterlife.
rows.anchor: الموت الذي عنده تنقطع العاجلة عنكم وتنتقلون إلى لآجلة التي تبقون فيها مخلدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject that reaches the collarbones is the soul, inferred from the verse despite lacking an earlier mention.
rows.anchor: أي الروح وجاز وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لان الآية تدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tarāqī are the bones flanking the hollow at the throat, the plural of tarquwah.
rows.anchor: العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال جمع ترقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever is not left neglected, without commands or prohibitions, resurrection, or recompense.
rows.anchor: أيحسب الكافران يترك مهملا لا يؤمر ولا ينهى ولا يبعث ولا يجازي

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read the verb with yāʾ: the semen is poured into the womb.
rows.anchor: بالياء ابن عامر وحفص أي يراق المنى في الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With tāʾ, the verb refers back to the drop (nutfah).
rows.anchor: في الرحم وبالتاء يعود إلى النطقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who performed these acts is able to bring the dead back to life.
rows.anchor: اليس الفعال لهذه الاشياء بقادر على الاعادة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When reciting this verse, the Prophet would answer, Glory be to You, indeed; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قراها يقول سبحانك ببلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi classifies Sūrat al-Insān as Meccan and says it has thirty-one verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الانسان مكية وهي احدى وثلاثون آية

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَنزِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the pronoun after the named subject adds emphasis upon emphasis.
rows.anchor: تكرير الضمير بعد إيقاهم اسما لأن تأكيد على تأكيد

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَنزِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction stresses that Allah alone sends the Qurʾān, reassuring the Prophet that its gradual revelation is wise and purposeful, including the command to persevere.
rows.anchor: بمعنى اختصاص الله بالتنزيل ليستقر فين فس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه إذا كان هو المنزل لم يكن تنزيله مفرقا إلا حكمة وصوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses showed Pharaoh the staff, or the staff and the shining hand, since together they count as one sign.
rows.anchor: أي فذهب فأرى موسى فرعون العصا أو العصا واليد البيضاء لأنهما فى حكم آية واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The events just mentioned are a lesson for whoever fears Allah.
rows.anchor: ﴾ المذكور ﴿ لعبرة لمن يخشى ﴾ الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to people who deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أأنتم ﴾ يا منكرى البعث ﴿ أشد خلقا ﴾ أصعب خلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate after al-samāʾ is omitted: the question means whether the sky is harder to create.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ محذوف الخبر أى أم السماء أشد خلقا ثم بين كيف خلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted subject of built it is Allah; the next verse explains how He built the sky.
rows.anchor: ثم بين كيف خلقها فقال ﴿ بناها ﴾ أى الله ثم بين البناء فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He raised the sky's roof high.
rows.anchor: ﴿ رفع سمكها ﴾ أعلى سقفها وقيل جعل مقدار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation says its vertical extent is immense, a distance of five hundred years.
rows.anchor: وقيل جعل مقدار ذهابها فى سمت العلو رفيعا مسيرة خمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He made the sky even, with no cracks or fissures.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فسواها ﴾ فعدلها مستوية بلا شقوق ولا فطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He brought out the earth's water by causing springs to gush, and its pasture means its forage.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أخرج منها ماءها ﴾ بتفجير العيون ﴿ ومرعاها ﴾ كلأها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi notes that no coordinating conjunction precedes akhraja.
rows.anchor: ولذا لم يدخل العاطف على أخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, akhraja is a circumstantial clause with an implicit qad.
rows.anchor: أو أخرج حال باضمار قد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did this to provide enjoyment and provision for people and their livestock.
rows.anchor: فعل ذلك تمتيعا لكم ولانعامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet frowned and turned away.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عبس ﴾ كلح أى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ وتولى ﴾ أعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks what could make the Prophet know the blind man's condition.
rows.anchor: وأى شىء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man might purify himself by hearing the Prophet and shedding the stain of ignorance.
rows.anchor: لعل الاعمى يتطهر بما يسمع منك من دنس الجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yazakkā derives from yatazakkā, with tāʾ assimilated into zāy.
rows.anchor: وأصله يتزكى فأدغمت التاء فى الزاى وكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhdhakkar means to take heed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أو يذكر ﴾ يتعظ ﴿ فتنفعه ﴾ نصبه عاصم

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Nasafi attributes the accusative reading to ʿĀṣim, notes al-Aʿshā, and construes it as a response to laʿalla.
rows.anchor: نصبه عاصم غير الأعشى جوابا للعل

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other readers use the nominative, coordinating the verb with yadhdhakkar.
rows.anchor: وغيره رفعه عطفا على يذكر ﴿ الذكرى ﴾ ذكراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhikrā means the Prophet's reminder or admonition.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذكرى ﴾ ذكراك اى موعظتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot know whether the man will purify himself or take heed; knowing that prospect would have prevented his neglect.
rows.anchor: أى انك لا تدى ما هو مترقب منه من تزك أو تذكر ولو دريت لما فرط ذلك منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for making the man accept Islam and purify himself; his duty is only to deliver the message.
rows.anchor: وليس عليك بأس فى أن يتزكى بالاسلام ان عليك إلا البلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man hurries to the Prophet in pursuit of good.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأما من جاءك يسعى ﴾ يسرع فى طلب الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that he fears Allah.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهو يخشى ﴾ الله أو الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he fears the unbelievers' harm as he comes to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أو الكفار أى اذاهم فى اتيانك أو الكبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Or he is wary of stumbling, as is customary for blind people.
rows.anchor: أو الكبوة كعادة العميان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative through an implied verb yassara, meaning He then made the way easy.
rows.anchor: نصب السبيل باضمار يسر أى ثم سهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God facilitated the way out of the mother's womb.
rows.anchor: له سبيل الخروج من بطن أمه أو بين له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God made the way of good and evil clear to him.
rows.anchor: أو بين له سبيل الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should consider the food he eats and lives by, and how God arranged its provision.
rows.anchor: الذى يأكله ويحيا به كيف دبرنا أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God split the earth open with vegetation growing through it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم شققنا الأرض شقا ﴾ بالنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grain includes wheat, barley, and other crops used for food.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأنبتنا فيها حبا ﴾ كالبر والشعير وغيرهما مما يتغذى به

rows.speaker: مدنى وشامى وعاصم وسهل ويعقوب
rows.claim: Madinan, Syrian, ʿĀṣim, Sahl, and Yaʿqūb read nushirat with lightening (takhfīf).
rows.anchor: فتحت بالتخفيف مدنى وشامى وعاصم وسهل ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls are records of deeds, folded at a person's death and opened when that person is judged.
rows.anchor: والمراد صحف الأعمال تطوى صحيفة الانسان عند موته ثم تنشر إذا حوسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the scrolls are distributed among their owners.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد نشرت بين أصحابها أى فرقت بينهم
